transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?
Hello, doctor. Thank you for seeing me. I'm here because I feel like I lose control around food at night and just keep eating even when I tell myself to stop.
Can you describe what happens at night that makes you feel like you lose control over eating, and is this behavior limited to nighttime or does it also happen during the day?

It really only happens late at night, especially when I'm alone and restless or after a stressful doctor's appointment. Once I get started, it feels like a switch flips in my brain where I tell myself, "Alejandro, basta," but my hands just keep piling food and I can't stop, even though I'm not actually hungry.
Do you usually feel guilty or ashamed after these late-night eating episodes, or do you feel more like you're in a trance and not fully aware of what you're doing until afterwards?

I feel deeply ashamed of how much I eat, which is why I wait for my wife to go to sleep so I can hide in the kitchen and eat in secret. During the episode, I'm actually aware of what I'm doing and even tell myself "Alejandro, basta," but I feel completely powerless to stop my hands from putting more food on my plate.

Can you tell me if during these episodes, you actually enjoy the taste of the food or if you're eating so quickly and automatically that you're not really paying attention to the taste or sensation of eating?

It feels completely automatic, and I'm not really tasting or enjoying the food at all. Once I start, that switch in my brain just flips off, and my hands keep piling food and putting it in my mouth. I just feel completely unable to stop, even though I'm not even savoring what I'm eating.
Do you recall any specific thoughts or emotions right before these episodes start, or is it more of a sudden urge to eat without any preceding thoughts or feelings?

It's usually not a sudden urge, but rather feeling very restless after a quiet day of writing, or anxious and worried about my heart health, especially after a cardiology appointment. The pressure and stress of being told to restrict my diet also weighs heavily on me, which leads me to wander into the kitchen.

Can you describe in more detail what you mean by 'a switch flips in your brain' during these episodes, and do you recall everything that happens during the episode afterwards, or are there parts that you don't remember?

By "a switch flips," I mean that even though I hear myself saying "Alejandro, basta," my hands just keep piling food onto the plate until everything is gone. I remember the entire episode very clearly afterward, including all the specific foods I ate, so I don't experience any memory loss or blackouts.
Can you estimate how often these episodes of feeling like you've lost control over eating happen in a typical week?

These late-night episodes have been happening at least a couple of times every week. They usually occur on the nights after I have a doctor's appointment or when my wife is away helping care for her sister.

Can you clarify if, during these episodes, you are aware of the amount of food you're consuming and if you're eating rapidly, as this might help differentiate between an eating disorder and another condition?

Yes, I am very aware of the massive amount because I remember the details clearly, like eating a whole pot of arroz con pollo, half a tray of roasted vegetables, bread, and ice cream straight from the carton. I might not be eating at a frantic speed, but I consume all of this in just an hour or two while feeling completely unable to stop my hands from piling food.

Do you experience any physical symptoms, such as nausea, abdominal pain, or vomiting, after these episodes of excessive eating, or do you typically feel physically uncomfortable but without any specific symptoms?

I don't experience any nausea or vomiting, but the physical discomfort afterward is very intense. My stomach feels extremely tight, stretched, and heavy, as if I have swallowed a rock. It actually hurts to stand up or bend over, so I just have to lean back in my chair and take shallow breaths.
Have you ever used compensatory behaviors, such as self-induced vomiting, laxatives, or excessive exercise, to try to counteract the calories consumed during these episodes?
No, doctor, I have never tried to throw up, use laxatives, or exercise excessively to get rid of the food. I have never used any of those methods to try to make up for what I ate.
Can you think of any times when you felt this loss of control over eating during the day, or is it exclusively happening at night?

It happens almost exclusively at night or late in the evening. During the day, I am usually busy with my writing or my wife is around, so I don't feel that urge. But late at night, when I am alone and restless or after she has gone to bed, that is when the loss of control hits me.
